Team 13's slot column is unchanged: Josh Allen slot 0 and starting and NOT being asked for, Lamar Jackson slot 20 on their bench, Travis Kelce at 178.1 in their slot-23 flex. open.thesis: Lawrence is the starting quarterback from week 2, benching Stafford. Confirmed by week 1 rather than assumed: 18 of 23, 245 yards, four touchdowns in three quarters against Stafford's 4.1. ESPN has Lawrence QB9 and Stafford unranked, so projection and reporting agree for once. HELD 14 Sep 16:40. Unchanged and unexecuted - nothing on the roster is droppable or swappable until rosters unlock, so this stays a WHEN_UNLOCKED card. Week 2 context added: Jacksonville-Denver opened at a 44.5 total with Jacksonville a slight underdog. Sources disagree on the venue (SI has Denver travelling to Jacksonville, the Yahoo odds piece has Jacksonville in Denver) and the league file carries no week 2 venues; priced as the road version.

open.thesis: REVERSED IN TIMING 14 Sep 16:40, not in direction. This morning's card said drop Mayer the moment rosters unlock. Today's reporting moves the modal Bowers return to week 3: Schefter has the Raiders believing there is a realistic chance he misses only one game, but Dr Deepak Chona, reading the same meniscus trim, says a ~2-week ramp is possible while the data make week 3 more likely, and the closest comparable (Gallup 2019) cost 19 days and two games. If Bowers returns week 3, Mayer starts for Las Vegas once more, and IPADE's flex takes a tight end, so that week has real value. He scored 9.2 on a 9.3 projection. The roster maths against him is unchanged - 85.0 season, lowest on the roster - but it is a projection argument and the reporting now points the other way for one week. Published as a ghost card. Also note: nothing was droppable today regardless, so no action was foregone.

open.playerName: Cam Little and the Jaguars D/ST
open.thesis: Required kicker and D/ST comparison, both answered hold. Little at 146.1 season is the highest-projected kicker available to this roster - ahead of Cairo Santos 143.2, Boswell 142.1 and Reichard 141.8 - and returned 12.0 in week 1. The Jaguars D/ST returned 12.0 with five sacks and rank 4th for week 2 despite the Denver draw, above Baltimore's 5th, which is the opposite of what seasonProj says (Baltimore 125.7, Jacksonville 103.9). Taking the week 2 rankings over the season field. Both are waiver claims here and priority never resets, so a stream would have to clear a much higher bar than a projection gap.
open.falsifiedIf: Little finishes outside the top 20 kickers across weeks 2-4, or the Jaguars D/ST finishes outside the top 12 in week 2.

open.thesis: Declined the largest ownership anomaly in the league on purpose and recorded it so a future run does not 'discover' it. Nix is 88.1% owned and carries status FREEAGENT at 295.3 season. The free-agent status is an artifact: every free agent in both leagues right now is a Kansas City or Denver player, because theirs is the only game that has not kicked off, and at 00:15Z they all become waiver claims. Declined because (a) nothing on the roster is droppable until rosters unlock, so the free window is unreachable, (b) by then he costs non-resetting priority, and (c) a third quarterback is not what this roster needs while the Jackson trade is live.
open.falsifiedIf: Lawrence's role wobbles in weeks 2-3 AND Nix is still unrostered in this league as a free agent rather than a waiver claim.

open.thesis: PRESERVED, NOT RECOMMENDED. Carried from the 13:18Z run and re-checked against the fresh snapshot: Team 13 really do carry two defences, and they have them the wrong way round - Seahawks 126.5 starting at slot 16, Texans 132.6 benched at slot 20. So Golden for the Texans D/ST is a second shape worth asking about if they decline Lamar Jackson. NOT published this run for one reason: I did not research the Houston defence in this session, and the standing rule is that no player is named in the output without a search behind him. It is also in tension with this run's hold-the-Jaguars-D/ST call, which rests on week 2 rankings rather than on the seasonProj field the trade maths would use.
open.falsifiedIf: Team 13 start the Texans D/ST, drop one defence, or accept the Jackson offer, any of which retires this.

The Tuten-for-Lamar proposal is withdrawn in favour of the Golden-for-Allen version. Season projections later confirmed its own stated risk: Tuten 205.2 against Lloyd 135.6, so the swap the weekly model called free was seventy points of season value.

Michael Mayer thesis FALSIFIED, exactly as its condition predicted and three weeks early. Schefter reports Bowers returns at the Chargers in week 2, which ends the role the add was made for. Mayer scored 9.2 and projects 85.0 for the season, the lowest on the roster. He is the drop the moment the week rolls and players unlock. The thesis was sound when written and the falsification condition did its job — this is the log working, not a mistake.

Trevor Lawrence hold resolved RIGHT and decisively. Lawrence 18 of 23 for 245 and four touchdowns, a 150.6 rating and 25.6 fantasy points in three quarters of a 34-10 win; Stafford returned 4.1 the same week. The thesis said Lawrence starts from week 2 and that is now a published card. Closing this and opening the lineup thesis in its place.

The 13:18Z 14 Sep run published IPADE with no roster block, no matchup header, no leagueName or teamName and no whatWentWrong section - the app had nothing to render for the team. It would also fail the current validator. Rebuilt in full at 16:40 in the nine-section schema.

Kicker slot Little->Boswell (8 Sep) -> Boswell->Little (10 Sep) came out right on the week - Little 12.0, Boswell 7.0 - and is still logged as churn. Being right about a reversal made for no stated reason is luck, and recording it as a win would teach the wrong lesson.
